title: 2FFS: 2-fidelity best-arm identification for minimax tree search
claim: A recursive decision procedure resolves the best choice by decomposing into root test, node-level recursion, and local selection rules.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, tree diagrams with dashed dividers and recursion arrows
description: Three-panel figure separated by dashed vertical lines. The left panel, 'Root decision', shows a root node r with child arms a1, a2, a_t (leader, blue), b_t (challenger, teal) and a_m, each with confidence intervals drawn as dot-line segments. A green-tick 'Condition holds' branch leads to 'stop at a_t'. A red 'Condition not met' branch leads to refining the coarser unresolved side, using L_at and U_bt boxes. The middle panel, 'Recursive resolve at node (v,s,k)', shows node v with children u1..ud, and a highlighted child u_j. Three branches are labelled slow sample for a leaf or exhausted budget, fast expand for an unexpanded node, and otherwise keep recursing. Each has a turtle or rabbit icon. Dashed arrows return the certificate. The right panel, 'Scale-k witness rule', has four small trees for the MIN/MAX selector and comparison cases. Blue highlights mark the chosen child. Gray tones and crossed marks mark the rejected ones.
caption: Algorithmic pipeline for 2-fidelity fast-slow (2FFS) minimax tree search.
abstract: We study fixed-confidence best-arm identification (BAI) in stochastic minimax trees. This problem is increasingly relevant in modern AI planning, where deep minimax search and Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with language model long rollouts face a fundamental tradeoff: heuristic evaluations are cheap but biased, while accurate rollouts are reliable but prohibitively expensive. We propose 2FFS, a two-fidelity tree-search algorithm that brings multi-fidelity flat bandit ideas into trees. The algorithm combines minimax-style fast expansion with MCTS-style stochastic sampling, adaptively deciding when to exploit cheap biased evaluations and when to invoke expensive accurate evaluations for local certification. We prove fixed-confidence correctness, establish finite stopping for exact identification, and give a polynomial-depth cost upper bound for general-depth trees. Across numerical stochastic-tree experiments, 2FFS uses substantially fewer samples and computational operations comparing to existing BAI-MCTS baseline.
